mstts:express-as.prosody:
Have you ever wondered why some conversations just flow, while others seem to stumble over invisible obstacles? Every day, we’re surrounded by hints—little signals and unspoken motivations—that shape the way we connect with the people around us. What if you could start to see the world through a new lens, one that reveals what’s really driving those choices, reactions, and relationships?
That’s exactly the journey we’re about to embark on together, inspired by Anne Bogel’s thoughtful book, Reading People: How Seeing the World through the Lens of Personality Changes Everything. In these pages, Anne opens the door to the fascinating world of personality frameworks—drawing from both ancient wisdom and modern psychology—to help us understand the why behind what people do, think, and feel.
As we explore ideas like Myers-Briggs, the Enneagram, and more, you’ll start to notice how these systems aren’t just about putting people into boxes. Instead, they’re maps for navigating the beautiful complexity of human nature. You’ll find yourself seeing everyday situations in a whole new light—whether you’re at work, at home, or just reflecting on your own thoughts.
Together, we’ll discover how recognizing patterns of temperament and preference can turn confusion into clarity, and misunderstandings into empathy. So, let’s dive in and see how the lens of personality can help us build deeper connections—with others, and with ourselves.
